answer: Under Regulation 18, every credit rating agency must: (a) make public the definitions of the concerned rating along with the symbol; (b) state that the ratings do not constitute recommendations to buy, hold or sell any securities; and (2) make available to the general public information relating to the rationale of the ratings, covering an analysis of various factors justifying a favourable assessment as well as factors constituting a risk.

citations.quote: Regulation 18: (1) Every credit rating agency — (a) shall make public the definitions of the concerned rating, along with the symbol and, (b) shall also state that the ratings do not constitute recommendations to buy, hold or sell any securities. answer: According to Securities and exchange board of india investment advis (in force since 2013-01-01): "25-11-2025 by SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025): individuals registered as investment advisers whose number of clients exceed three hundred at any point of time or the fee collected during the financial year exceeds three crore rupees, whichever is earlier shall — (i) immediately intimate the Administration and Supervisory Body and initiate the process of transition from individual to non-individual investment adviser; and (ii) apply for grant of in-principle approval for registration as non-individual investment adviser within 3 months from the date on which the threshold is reached."

answer: As of 2020-01-01, the minimum eligibility criteria are: (a) corporate form: the applicant is set up and registered as a company under the Companies Act, 2013; (b) business objects: the applicant has, in its Memorandum of Association, specified rating activity as one of its main objects; (c) net worth: the applicant has a minimum net worth of rupees twenty five crore.
